description: SwiftData workout app. The latest commit plants one defect per swift-reviewer check (observation, locked-history write, Character-based CSV line splitting, unstyled row buttons, two presentations on one view, a missing brace) next to look-alike code that is correct.
prompt: Review the changes in the most recent commit (git show HEAD) for correctness and report your findings.

must_find.why: Holds the Session model directly and renders counts from the to-many sets, with no dependency on a bumped scalar such as session.updatedAt, so toggling a set may not re-render the header.
Overwrites weight on a recorded (locked) session instead of appending a SetCorrection; the doc comment says it is for recorded workouts.
Iterates Characters; "\r\n" is one grapheme that equals neither "\n" nor "\r", so CRLF files come back as one line.
Two Buttons in a row rendered inside a List (LiveSessionView) with no .buttonStyle(.borderless): one tap fires both.
A .sheet and a .fileImporter on the same view, driven by separate booleans.
The VStack opened on line 8 is never closed; .padding() attaches inside it.

must_not_flag.why: Appending a correction to a locked session is the supported path.
Character iteration over a name, not line splitting; graphemes are correct here.
Braces inside a string literal; a naive count flags them but they are not code.
Base-commit file, unchanged by HEAD and correct.

note: Decoys are scoped to the pitfall they imitate: a `correctness` finding on the same code is scored as unlabeled, not as a decoy hit.
